title: Residual-dimension obstructions for null-projected supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories — submission package
description:
Residual-dimension obstructions for null-projected supersymmetric Yang-Mills theories. Version 2.1.1 holds the fourth version of the Hexagon preprint in the folder hexagon-v4 (NullProjectedSYM_v4.pdf, 35 pages, its TeX ZIP with the Python programs in anc/, unpacked source, arXiv tarball, Hexagon portal fields and AI provenance file), replacing https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v3. The Main Theorem is now a classification: a null-projected super Yang-Mills theory with a Majorana-Weyl gaugino and k null vectors exists in signature (s,t) if and only if s+t-2k = 10 and s-t in {8, 0, -8}, or s+t-2k = 2 and s = t (Corollary 5.15). Sufficiency comes from Theorem 5.12 (Nishino's theories carried by a complex isometry to every signature with residual dimension ten, among them 9+9 and 9+17) and Theorem 5.14 (theories with residual dimension two in every (k+1)+(k+1), with vanishing cubic terms and off-shell closure). Theorem 7.3 shows that no contraction of the source rescues the signatures (11+8n)+3 and their companions with n >= 1, including 27+3, and Proposition 7.5 that several gauginos with their own parameters do not either. Appendices E and F check these results with contraction_check.py (32 checks) and residual_two_check.py (50 checks). Citations of unrefereed preprints were replaced by published versions or removed.

Theories with auxiliary fields, nonlinear transformation rules, gauginos mixed by their transformation rules or a non-Lie gauge structure lie outside these results; Remark 7.6 explains why no statement about the superalgebra alone can exclude every theory.

Verification scope: No general Lean formalisation is claimed. The proofs are written in the manuscript; the gamma-matrix calculations are supplementary finite numerical checks.

Earlier preprint versions: https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v1, https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v2 and https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v3. Version 2.1.1 removes the note that followed the abstract; the mathematics is that of version 2.1.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23788708. Version 2.0.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23787988, holds an earlier package of the fourth version.
